current_exact_evidence.root_cause: Pinned FLEURS fixture can materialize as IEEE-float WAV while the current comparator validation/VAD path requires PCM16 mono 16 kHz; failure occurs before Nemotron transcription or ASR-quality measurement.

fresh_primary_source_findings.finding: Python 3.13 stdlib wave supports uncompressed PCM only; IEEE-float WAV format-tag 3 is not a portable admitted input on that runtime.
Python 3.15 adds IEEE-float WAV support, so changing Python version would alter the runtime subject rather than repair the fixture contract minimally.
FLEURS exposes decoded audio as float arrays at 16 kHz; fixture serialization therefore needs an explicit deterministic encoding contract instead of assuming PCM16 source bytes.
WebRTC VAD accepts 16-bit mono PCM at 8/16/32/48 kHz with fixed 10/20/30 ms frame sizes; PCM16 mono 16 kHz is therefore a direct compatible boundary.
NeMo ASR audio preprocessing defaults to 16 kHz, aligning the comparator's desired normalized fixture rate with the model preprocessing contract.

hypothesis_fusion.H1: The narrow repair should normalize the already-pinned decoded fixture to deterministic mono 16 kHz PCM16 and preserve original-source and normalized-fixture digests separately.
hypothesis_fusion.H2: Upgrading Python merely to make stdlib wave accept float WAV is a worse discriminator because it changes environment semantics and does not satisfy the downstream VAD PCM16 ABI by itself.
hypothesis_fusion.H3: The repair must not change FLEURS row selection, references, Nemotron model/runtime identities, RNNT right-context axis, scoring thresholds, or receipt semantics.
hypothesis_fusion.counterhypothesis: After normalization, a separate model-load, ASR-quality, latency, receipt-contract, or product failure may emerge; none is supported yet.
hypothesis_fusion.decision: Route one fixture-only repair to Trigger4, then execute one exact nonduplicate comparator run.
